source.title: Revisiting Who’s Harry Potter: Towards Targeted Unlearning from a Causal Intervention Perspective
source.authors: Yu-Jian Liu; Yang Zhang; T. Jaakkola; Shi-Yu Chang

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning efficacy and tests unlearned models under jailbreak, language, and alias variations, using its own targeted-unlearning method and measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports targeted-unlearning efficacy under many-shot and embedding-space jailbreaks, plus Spanish/French and alias prompt variations. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, or quantization. Figure 4 and Appendix Figure A1 report normalized efficacy and utility, but their flattened values do not support reliable assignment of individual chart values here.
record.test_reason: The study unlearns 2 persons from Llama2-7b-chat with 8 methods, including its own, plus a re-implementation of WHP (an original source). It then measures forget-QA unlearning efficacy under many-shot jailbreaking, an embedding-space attack, Spanish/French translation and aliases (Tables A8, A9). These are prompt-side recovery attempts aimed at the same question, whether forgetting survives attack. It is a different method and dataset from the originals, so T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that their causal-intervention framework justifies and extends WHP and is competitive on all five targeted-unlearning criteria without retain data. They add that most methods generalize to Spanish/French and aliases, while the two jailbreaks degrade efficacy more, especially for training-free PROMPT. They caution there is no theoretical guarantee and that robustness conclusions hold only for the two attacks tested.
record.recipe_differences: The proposed method extends the name-change approach by averaging multiple counterfactual distributions, changing the replacement name back in outputs, and using an explicit counterfactual prompt. The WHP baseline is reimplemented without reinforcement bootstrapping.
record.method_sensitivity: Jailbreak type changes reported efficacy; translated language also changes efficacy for some methods. The paper separately reports that aggregating more replacement-name distributions affects hallucination avoidance and retrained-model approximation.

fits_no_version.finding: Aggregating more counterfactual teacher distributions raises the rate of 'I don't know' rejections (hallucination avoidance) but makes the model less like a retrained model on TOFU.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning methods trade off refusal-style forgetting against fidelity to a retrained-from-scratch model.

fits_no_version.finding: Across all methods and learning rates, unlearning efficacy correlates -0.72 with model utility and 0.87 with adversarial robustness (Figure A4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stronger forgetting, including under attack, generally costs model utility in targeted unlearning.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors note that there is no theoretical guarantee of unlearning and that robustness conclusions pertain only to the two tested jailbreak attacks. Table A8 and Table A9 provide no uncertainty estimates. The results do not establish a chance-level reference for the efficacy scores.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 and Appendix Figure A1 report normalized criteria for multiple methods, but the flattened chart text does not reliably assign all displayed values to individual conditions. Other findings in the text about general utility and response quality are not included as rows here because they are not recovery-attack outcomes.

untested.parts: No chance-level or pre-unlearning efficacy reference. Only two jailbreaks plus language and alias probes, not the full set of simple attacks.
Entirely untested: no relearning or fine-tuning recovery.
Entirely untested: no activation ablation or probing of whether knowledge is blocked or deleted.
No general paraphrasing or rephrasing, no in-context information, and no languages beyond Spanish and French.
The proposed method is not tested against relearning, internal edits or quantization.

missing.what: Model utility and response quality per method, needed for A's 'keeps general ability'. PROMPT and PROMPT-DISTILL have low utility, GA produces gibberish, and Ours keeps high utility.
Adversarial robustness (minimum efficacy under the two jailbreaks) for the forget-20 and forget-100 person settings
Adversarial robustness on Llama-3-8b-instruct for NPO, PROMPT-DISTILL and Ours
RLHF (SFT/SFT+DPO) abstention baseline: efficacy and adversarial robustness
TOFU forget quality (KS-test p-value vs retrained model) against model utility; most baselines, including WHP, have p<0.05
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Figure 5; Appendix F, Figure A5

record.verdict_notes: Efficacy is the harmonic mean of 1-ROUGE and the GPT privacy score on forget QA; higher means more forgetting. The original model's efficacy is not reported, though forget QA was filtered to questions it answered correctly. The embedding-space attack is a white-box optimized soft prompt, so linking it to E (prompting only) is a stretch; a researcher may prefer to treat it separately. WHP is re-implemented without reinforcement bootstrapping, so WHP rows test that re-implementation rather than the original source's exact recipe. No uncertainty is reported for Tables A8 and A9; alias results cover only 9 persons.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures efficacy and utility, but does not state a chance-level reference for its reported efficacy scores. It tests two jailbreaks, not the full range of simple recovery attacks.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or internal-edit recovery test.
The study tests many-shot and embedding-space jailbreaks, translated questions, and aliases. It does not test arbitrary rephrasing or other languages beyond Spanish and French.
The proposed method is tested against two jailbreak attacks and language/alias variations, not against fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, or quantization.

tranche.reason: A different method (a counterfactual-intervention extension of WHP) on the same unlearning question, with its own attack tests.

source_check.notes: All 25 rows match Tables A8/A9 (WPU, 2 persons, Llama2-7b-chat). The baselines are each unlearned model's efficacy on English queries; no pre-unlearning reference is given, and GA's high efficacy reflects gibberish output. Four statements (A.method_sensitivity[2], F.support[5], F.against[16], F.method_sensitivity[6]) cite this study's rows but say nothing about it. Whether training-free PROMPT counts for A/E is an owner call.
